title: Measuring Heterogeneity in TV Advertising Elasticities: Evidence from 135 Retail and Restaurant Brands
eligible_reason: Main design is a continuous-treatment TWFE (own and competitor ad stock, store FE + state-week FE, brand by brand). The only binary DiD is a validation exercise for 36 brands that run isolated one-week local ad pulses (treatment switches on and off within a week), compared with never-advertised DMAs using the Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation event study; results appear only in the Web Appendix (main text reports just the pre-trend F-test, F = .89, p = .53). No main-text binary staggered-adoption specification.
design_notes: Store-week panel 2019-2022 (SafeGraph Spend revenue, Nielsen Ad Intel GRP). Baseline: log(Sales_it) = b_own f(AS_bdt) + b_comp f(AS_cdt) + store FE + brand-state-week FE, two-way clustered DMA and week, estimated separately for each of 135 brands; ad stock continuous with decay 0.9. Extensions: border-county design, heterogeneity interactions, curvature (polynomials, B-splines, Hill), counterfactual reallocation. BJS event study around ad pulses is Web Appendix only and the treatment is transient.
estimators_reported: TWFE with continuous ad-stock treatment (store FE, state-week FE)
Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation event study (Web Appendix only, pulse treatment)
screener_notes: Data availability statement: all data except US Census are proprietary (Nielsen Ad Intel via Kilts Center, SafeGraph Spend); a synthetic dataset was shared with the JMR data editor under an approved alternative disclosure plan. Not eligible: continuous treatment in all main-text tables (Tables 1-7); the BJS DiD is appendix-only and uses a one-week pulse that switches off.
